results.target_claim: Tough on stains, kinder to our planet
results.target_reason: In our assessment the claim is misleading. The ASA upheld the complaint, finding the basis of 'kinder' was not made clear and that it had not seen evidence of the product's overall life-cycle impact versus Persil's earlier products or other products. The ASA did not find the specific features false (30C quick washes, bottles with 50% recycled plastic excluding cap and label), and Unilever said it was disappointed with the ruling. We found the phrase absent from the current Persil UK pages we fetched, but that does not prove it has been withdrawn.
results.target_rule: ASA BCAP Code 3.1, 3.9, 9.2, 9.4, 9.5 (as applied in the ruling; the non-broadcast equivalent is CAP Code section 11). Under the UK CMA Green Claims Code, our assessment is that it fails the principles on clear and unambiguous claims, full life cycle and substantiation. Under EU Directive 2024/825 (applies from 27 Sep 2026), generic claims of this kind would be tested against the ban on generic environmental claims without recognised excellent environmental performance. That is our inference, and the Directive did not apply to the 2022 UK ad.

results.target_claim: Vague sustainability claims and claims about SAF and reforestation (15 of 19 statements). Examples quoted in the judgment (KLM 'Fly Responsibly' ads): "Join us in creating a more sustainable future"; "Sustainable jet fuel: a promising solution"; "With our CO2ZERO service, you can reduce the impact of your flight on the environment"; "sustainable jet fuel… reduces CO2 emissions by at least 75%"
results.target_reason: In our assessment, the Amsterdam District Court (ECLI:NL:RBAMS:2024:1512) found 15 of 19 expressions misleading and unlawful under the Dutch Unfair Commercial Practices Act: 'more sustainable' statements were vague and general, 'sustainable' for SAF was too absolute and painted too rosy a picture given SAF's very small share, 'CO2ZERO' was an absolute term not justified by the offsetting link, and 'at least 75%' was insufficiently substantiated. The court did not uphold 4 of the 19 (nos. 5, 9, 11, 13) and ordered only a declaration plus costs (EUR 18,211.53), refusing an injunction because the ads were no longer run. Under the UK CMA Green Claims Code we would expect the same wording to be at high risk; under EU Directive 2024/825 (to apply from 27 Sept 2026) generic environmental claims and offset-based neutral/reduced-impact product claims are prohibited.
results.target_rule: Dutch Unfair Commercial Practices Act (implementing Directive 2005/29/EC), as applied in the ruling; UK CMA Green Claims Code (by analogy); EU Directive 2024/825 (applies from 27 Sept 2026). The EU Green Claims Directive is only a pending proposal and is not relied on.
